messages.subject: discrete lower-bound truncation bug
parts:
There's a serious bug in the way the contribution to
the log density of the normalization term induced by
the truncation for discrete distribution lower bounds.

Instead of treating the bound L as inclusive in
T[L, U] and T[L, ], it is being normalized in such
a way that L is exclusive and U is inclusive.

Upper bounds for discrete distributions are OK and
all bounds for continuous distributions are OK.

This will be fixed for 2.12.

This will affect sampling and optimization for cases
where a discrete distribution has a parameter that's
declared as a parameter in the Stan model, e.g.,

parameters {
real<lower=0> lambda;

model {
y ~ poisson(lambda) T[4, ]; // *** BAD NORMALIZATION ***

There is no problem for upper bounds or continuous distributions.

- Bob
